AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md README.md business cache config.yaml data demo-video docs evals evidence hackathon.md pyproject.toml runs scripts site spendradar spikes tests uv.lock vid --- # Spend Radar **An agent that tells a finance team where competitors out-invest them in people, and shows its work.** Every number in its report has a source, and before reporting, the agent tries to disprove its own findings. Built solo by team **qwep** (Akarsh Dhingra) during **neatHack**, 10–12 Oct 2026. Uses **neatlogs** (tracing), **Entire** (checkpoints, code graph, trails and runners) and **cfo.ai** (business plan). > The company in the demo, *Acme Observability Inc.*, is **fictional**. Its finance files are generated by `scripts/make_acme_data.py`. The competitors are real; their data comes live from Crustdata. ![Spend Radar: a run, the self-audit, recovery decisions and the Entire chain, from the evidence site](docs/spend-radar.gif) **Evidence site (live):** https://akarsh-dhingra.github.io/SpeedRadar-NeetHack/ — every scored run, the before/after case studies, the neatlogs and Entire pages, and the cfo.ai plan. Each judging requirement is mapped on its overview page. Sample output: [`evidence/sample-report/report.md`](evidence/sample-report/report.md) (evidence run 1010-7bf26d). ## The problem Finance teams budget against their own ledger, not the market. They find out a competitor doubled its ML team, or that their own marketing team is out of line with peers, a quarter too late. The data exists (headcount by function, hiring, funding), but turning it into a budget comparison you can defend takes days of manual work. ## What the agent does, end to end **Input:** a folder of finance files (a budget spreadsheet, invoice PDFs, a spend policy, a salary table) and a list of competitors. **Output:** `runs//report.md`, which contains: - **per category** (engineering, ML/AI, sales, marketing): Acme's share of headcount vs the competitor median range, whether the policy is met, and the gap in people and dollars (an estimate) - **internal checks:** budget and invoice totals that don't add up, mis-categorised invoices, infra invoices over budget - an **Overturned claims** section, listing findings the agent disproved itself - a numbered **source for every number** (file + sheet/row/page, or Crustdata endpoint + field + fetch time) - the **recovery log** (what failed, the options, what the LLM chose, and what a fixed rule would have chosen) ## How it works ![Spend Radar loop](evidence/architecture.png) ```mermaid flowchart LR P[PLAN
LLM writes typed task list] --> C{coverage check} C --> A[ACT
one tool call] A --> O[OBSERVE
store value + source] O --> V{VERIFY
deterministic checks} V -- pass --> A V -- fail --> D[DECIDE:RECOVERY
LLM picks from fixed menu] D --> A A -- queue empty --> X[cross-document checks] X --> F[FINDINGS
maths in Python] F --> S[SELF-AUDIT
recompute · sources · contradictions
LLM verdict + 2nd-provider opinion] S --> R[REPORT
sourced, overturned claims listed] ``` **Who decides what.** - **The LLM decides:** the plan, which recovery action to take from a fixed menu (`reparse_alt`, `narrow_range`, `fetch_more_signal`, `substitute_competitor`, `mark_low_confidence`, `skip`), and the audit verdicts. - **Python decides:** how tasks run, **all arithmetic**, retry caps (3 per task), Crustdata credit caps (60 per run), and LLM quota. | Focus area | How it shows up | Trace | |---|---|---| | Planning | `plan` span: an LLM task list validated against a Pydantic schema; `verify:plan_coverage` adds anything the plan missed | `288f07d84bb84e15754a241eef40d779` | | Tool use | list_files, read_spreadsheet, read_pdf (text / LLM), crustdata_company, crustdata_jobs, classify_titles; each is a `TOOL` span | same | | State | `RunState` saved atomically after every step (`runs//state.json`); `resume` continues a killed run in the same neatlogs session | `522dfe5f0903595439c960a5e3b081c6` ([resume after crash](evidence/recovery/resume-after-crash.md)) | | Context | every figure keeps its source and the report cites it; each run also records its commit and Entire checkpoint; prompts are versioned templates on every LLM span | `93ce24c6097db7d0ab7d5b90e1dcba4b` | | Execution | one tool per task; tasks whose inputs aren't ready are deferred; every task outcome is a neatlogs `log()` step | `93ce24c6097db7d0ab7d5b90e1dcba4b` | | Recovery | `decide:recovery` spans record the options offered, the choice, the rule default, and the reason; fallback across models/providers; Crustdata backoff + stale-cache fallback; resume after a crash | `evidence/recovery/` | | Verification | totals within 1%, ≥ 2 independent signals, signal agreement, vendor-category consistency, no unsourced numbers | `verify:*` spans | | Iteration | five case studies with before/after runs; every change since 11 Oct reviewed on an Entire trail | `evidence/case-studies/`, [trails](https://entire.io/gh/akarsh-dhingra/SpeedRadar-NeetHack/trails/2) | **Confidence is computed, never typed in:** `confidence = checks × signals × freshness` (`spendradar/verify.py`). - `checks` = passed / total checks behind the finding. - `signals` = min(1, n_signals / 2) × agreement between signals. - `freshness` = 1 up to 90 days old, falling to 0.5 at 365 days. - An audit downgrade halves the score; content.text:
The CLI works on your machine: I ran `uv run python -m spendradar ledger` and it printed today's quota with nothing exhausted [proof: ran `spendradar ledger` this session]. Your `.env` is in place [proof: `ls -a` this session].

## How to run it on the call

**Before the call (5 min):**
1. Open the evidence site in a browser tab: https://akarsh-dhingra.github.io/SpeedRadar-NeetHack/. You can also open `site/index.html` locally [proof: README.md "See the evidence"]. It's your safety net, because it needs no API and nothing in it can fail live.
2. Open a finished report in VS Code: [evidence/sample-report/report.md](evidence/sample-report/report.md) [proof: `ls evidence/sample-report`].
3. Open your neatlogs dashboard and log in.

**Live on the call:**
```bash
uv run python -m spendradar run data/acme
```
This writes `runs/<id>/report.md` and `state.json` [proof: README "Run it yourself"; `ls runs/1011-f679dc`]. Crustdata responses come from the cache, so a run spends no credits; the cached runs in the README table show 0 credits [proof: README Results table]. I haven't timed a full run today {unverified}. Start it early and talk over it.

To show recovery, run this optional second command:
```bash
uv run python -m spendradar run data/acme --inject crustdata:429 --inject llm:429
```
It injects failures on purpose so they can watch the agent recover [proof: README "Run it yourself"].

## How to explain it (about 3 minutes)

**1. Problem (2 sentences).** Finance teams budget against their own books, not the market. They find out a competitor doubled its ML team a quarter too late.

**2. What it does.** It takes a folder of finance files (budget, invoice PDFs, spend policy, salary table) and a list of real competitors. It returns a report per category (engineering, ML/AI, sales, marketing) with:
- our numbers next to the competitor range
- the gap
- whether policy is broken
- a source for every number
- an "Overturned claims" section listing findings the agent disproved itself

Say clearly that Acme is fictional and the competitor data is real, pulled live from Crustdata [proof: README intro].

**3. The loop.** Show `evidence/architecture.png`: Plan → Act → Observe → Verify → (on failure) Decide:recovery → Self-audit → Report [proof: README "How it works"]. The line to land: **the LLM plans, picks recovery actions from a fixed menu, and gives audit verdicts. Python does all the maths, retry caps and credit caps.** Confidence comes from a formula in `spendradar/verify.py`; nobody types it in [proof: README].

**4. The three sponsor tools:**
- **neatlogs:** every LLM call, tool call, retry and recovery decision is traced, and every bug fix started from a trace. Show one `decide:recovery` span in the dashboard.
- **Entire:** commits carry checkpoints. `spendradar explain <trace_id>` goes from a failing neatlogs span to the code line to the Entire session and prompt that wrote it [proof: README "Entire" section].
- **cfo.ai:** the business plan uses measured cost per run: $0.0285 of LLM cost plus 20.8 Crustdata credits without the cache. In the Base scenario cash flow turns positive in month 15. Crustdata is about 99% of the cost of serving a customer, so caching decides the margin [proof: README "cfo.ai" + Results].

**5. Proof it works.** Every evidence run caught 5/5 planted errors with 0 unsupported numbers. Case study 02 cut competitor substitutions from 3 to 0 and credits from 26.6 to 5.4 [proof: README Results].

**6. Be upfront about the limits** (mentors respect this):
- The ML/AI estimate is the weakest, because Crustdata has no ML role, so it comes from classified job titles.
- Most case studies are n = 1 per side; only case study 05 has n = 5.
- Cost figures are paid-equivalent estimates, not real bills [proof: README Limitations].

## Likely questions
- *"Why not just ask an LLM?"* Because it would make numbers up. Here every number has a source, the maths runs in Python, and the agent tries to disprove its own findings before reporting.
- *"What happens when an API fails?"* It backs off and retries, falls back to the cache, then to another model or provider. Every hop shows up as a span. That's the `--inject` run.
- *"Who'd pay for this?"* Point to the pricing tiers in [business/cfoai_plan.md](business/cfoai_plan.md).

Your message cut off at "explain the". If you meant something specific, like the code or the business side, tell me and I'll go deeper on that part.

I do have some time, more than 12 to 20 hours for the hackathon to finish. What else can I improve upon? And the website that you made, shows everything, but it does not show what our project initially means. Like, I want to show like how it planned and acted in a very simple way. So maybe we can im- increase that. So let me know.
